title: AI Agents and the Fight for Customer Data

reader_summary.headline: Companies must keep all data in one place for AI agents to work effectively.
reader_summary.overview: The episode argues that businesses need unified data platforms because AI agents require full context to function. Vendors locking down access creates unnecessary costs and complexity. Companies should build their own data copies to stay current and avoid vendor restrictions.

key_points.text: Companies must keep all data in one place so AI agents have the necessary context to work effectively.
key_points.evidence_quote: There is a new reason to have all your data in one place, which is AI agency context.

key_points.text: Customers must build their own data platforms to keep data fresh and accessible regardless of vendor restrictions.
key_points.evidence_quote: It's very important for every company who wants to do things with data to create their own data platform where they have a copy of all of their own data and it's being kept continuously up to date.

key_points.text: Vendors that charge fees or block customers from taking their own data create unnecessary complexity and high costs for businesses.
key_points.evidence_quote: And the customers will still do it and they'll just work around these barriers at great cost and complexity.

key_points.text: AI agents are evolving to have their own identities and join existing human workflows like email and Slack.
key_points.evidence_quote: Now we're saying I actually set up open claw. That's great. I use nano claw.

key_points.text: Large companies should demand contracts that guarantee they can access and move their own data without restrictions.
key_points.evidence_quote: Number one, you should insist on having a copy of all of your own company data in a data lake that you control.

notes: Martin Casado speaks with George Fraser, cofounder and CEO of Fivetran, about the future of data infrastructure in the age of AI. The conversation covers Fivetran’s merger with dbt, the changing role of data platforms, and why Fraser believes many companies are overestimating the threat AI poses to enterprise software. They discuss open data access, the backlash against AI agents accessing systems of record, and why businesses still need centralized data foundations even as agent-based workflows become more common. Along the way, Fraser shares his views on data gravity, coding agents, enterprise AI adoption, and how AI is changing the way software companies build and operate products.
